messages:
From: Michael Lewis <michael.lewis@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLOs for Private VPC deployment

Hi Marissa / Aditya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good overview of Redwood's private VPC offering. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we scope capacity planning and our procurement timeline:

- Our product team is targeting a p95 response time for streaming generation of ~150ms for responses up to ~64 tokens.
- Expected steady-state concurrency: ~30 concurrent sessions, with short bursts up to 80 concurrent sessions.
- Peak sustained throughput estimate: ~400 requests/sec (mostly streaming chat completions).
- We prefer cloud-provider peering (Direct Connect equivalent) but can provision a site-to-site VPN if needed.
- Egress: all traffic will originate from our VPC in us-west-2 and must egress to Redwood endpoints in the same region; please call out any fixed egress IPs required.
- Internal latency budget on our side for request propagation is ~25ms; we need the end-to-end p95 to be <=150ms.

Attached is a simple network diagram and our initial SLO worksheet. Can you confirm whether those targets are achievable and what the recommended GPU footprint / concurrency per VM would look like? Also let us know any network tests or traces your team needs (traceroute/iperf) so we can coordinate with our networking team.

Thanks,
Michael Lewis
Head of Platform — Acme Corp

Attachment: network-diagram.pdf (diagram, 1 page)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs for Private VPC deployment - follow-up

Thanks Michael — appreciated. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size this correctly:

Recap of ask:
- p95 <= 150ms for streaming responses up to ~64 tokens.
- Steady concurrency ~30, bursts to ~80, throughput ~400 req/s (streaming).
- Preference: peering, fallback: site-to-site VPN.
- Egress from Acme us-west-2 to Redwood us-west-2.
- Internal latency budget: ~25ms.

Questions / requests:
1) Can you confirm whether the 150ms p95 is for first-byte latency (time to first token) or for complete response time? If streaming, we usually size around time-to-first-byte for SLO.
2) Are requests uniform in token length distribution (most <64 tokens), or do you expect a long-tail of large generations?
3) Is KV cache allowed/stored in your VPC, or will each request need cold model compute?
4) Please share a traceroute and an iperf window to Redwood's peering CIDR (we'll provide target IPs) — that'll help validate network RTTs.

Next steps from our side:
- Dev will run a quick feasibility calc and propose GPU VM sizing and batching configuration by EOD tomorrow.
- I'll share our performance SLO template (attached) and an initial checklist for peering/VPN requirements.

Attaching: slo_template.xlsx (Redwood SLO template)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Lewis <michael.lewis@acme.com>

Date: 2026-03-16T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs for Private VPC deployment - follow-up

Marissa — answers below (shared with our network owners as well):

1) The 150ms p95 target is for time-to-first-token (we're very latency sensitive for initial token). Subsequent token streaming can be looser.
2) Distribution: ~85% of requests will be <=64 tokens, 10% between 64-256, 5% >256.
3) KV cache: we can host a read-only customer-side cache in our VPC (Redis) if that helps; prefer caching for session state but model KV is under Redwood control.
4) Attaching our network contact (it-acme@acme.com) — they will run tests once you provide peering IPs. We prefer peering but can do VPN during initial proof-of-concept.

Other notes:
- Egress: our environment requires that outbound flows traverse our perimeter NAT; we will share the NAT public IPs.
- Internal latency budget: our application stack (LB + app) needs to keep <25ms additional latency — ideally your network RTT target to Redwood should be <10ms.

Happy to hop on a short follow-up call if it helps.

Thanks,
Michael

Looping in my quick feasibility notes after looking at the distribution and targets:

- Model/config: For streaming-first-token p95 <=150ms at ~400 req/s with the token distribution you provided, we recommend starting with 2 x A100-80GB (or equivalent accel) in a dedicated pool for the initial POC, with continuous batching disabled for first-token low-latency paths and aggressive streaming optimizations enabled.
- Concurrency handling: Each GPU with our runtime should comfortably handle ~120 concurrent streaming sessions with per-session small token outputs if batching is tuned for low latency; that aligns with your burst needs.
- Throughput: Sustained 400 req/s should be fine with the above, but we will want to monitor token-per-second and adjust autoscale to add an extra GPU at ~450-500 effective req/s.
- Network requirements: To hit end-to-end p95 <=150ms with your 25ms internal budget, we need network RTT from your app tier to our edge <10ms. Please coordinate to run traceroute + 60s iperf3 window to our peering IPs (we will share in a separate mail).
- KV/cache: Using customer-hosted Redis for session context is fine; model KV cache must remain on Redwood side for performance — we will keep warm caches for hot sessions during the POC.

Open items:
- We need a conservative estimate of average tokens generated per request for the 85% <64 bucket (mean tokens) — if that mean is closer to 40 vs 10, compute footprint changes.
- Please confirm whether TLS termination happens at your LB or at app instances (affects RTT).

I'll prepare a short benchmark plan and expected p95/p99 projections for the proposed 2xA100 pool and share tomorrow morning.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Principal Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference
